source: San Francisco Public Works Code Sec. 794, Autonomous Delivery Devices
definition: A motorized device that carries items on City sidewalks for commercial purposes, guided or controlled without a person sitting or standing on it and steering it.

rules.title: Sidewalks only
rules.text: The permit program covers City sidewalks. Streets and highways under SFMTA jurisdiction are outside it.

rules.title: PDR zoning only
rules.text: Testing is limited to sidewalks in PDR (Production, Distribution, Repair) zoning districts.

rules.title: Not on a high-injury corridor
rules.text: No testing on sidewalks along Vision Zero high-injury corridors.

rules.title: Room for people with disabilities
rules.text: The sidewalk must keep a path of travel for people with disabilities, or have an effective width of at least 6 feet.

rules.title: 3 mph speed limit
rules.text: A device may not go faster than 3 miles per hour.

rules.title: Human operator within 30 feet
rules.text: A human operator must stay within 30 feet of the device for the whole test.

rules.title: Yield to pedestrians and bicycles
rules.text: Devices must yield the right of way to pedestrians and bicycles.

rules.title: Obey signs and signals
rules.text: Devices must obey all traffic and pedestrian signs and signals.

rules.title: Headlights in low light
rules.text: Headlights must operate at night, sunrise and sunset.

rules.title: Warning noise
rules.text: A device must emit a warning noise while operating, loud enough for nearby pedestrians and cyclists.

rules.title: ID and contact details
rules.text: Each device must carry a unique identifier with the permittee's contact information.

rules.title: No waste or hazardous cargo
rules.text: Devices may not carry waste or hazardous materials, including flammables or ammunition.

rules.title: Docked on private property
rules.text: When not in use, a device must be docked on private property, not on the sidewalk or public right of way.

rules.title: Three devices per permit
rules.text: A permit may cover no more than three devices.

rules.title: Permit required
rules.text: Operating a device on a public sidewalk without a permit is unlawful.

rules.title: R&D testing only
rules.text: Permits cover research-and-development testing. Every other use is prohibited.

rules.title: 180-day term, two extensions
rules.text: A permit lasts up to 180 days, with at most two 90-day extensions.

rules.title: Nine devices citywide
rules.text: No more than nine devices may be permitted in the city at one time.

rules.title: One permit per permittee
rules.text: A permittee may hold one permit (a second only under a narrow exception, and it cannot be extended).

rules.title: Notice posted for 20 days
rules.text: Notice must be posted at the test sites for 20 days.

rules.title: Photo proof of notice
rules.text: The applicant must submit photo evidence that notice was posted.

rules.title: Public hearing
rules.text: The Director holds a public hearing on every application.

rules.title: No operating during an appeal
rules.text: The permittee may not operate devices while an appeal to the Board of Supervisors is pending.

rules.title: Stop procedure on file
rules.text: The application must include operations manuals, including how to bring the device to a full stop.

rules.title: Privacy policy on file
rules.text: The application must include a privacy policy for photo, video and other test data.

rules.title: Permit conditions met
rules.text: The Director may attach safety conditions. Breaking them can mean revocation and a bar on future permits.

rules.title: Insurance proof on hand
rules.text: Proof of general liability, automotive liability and workers' compensation insurance, readily accessible.

rules.title: City indemnified
rules.text: The permittee must agree to indemnify, defend and hold the City harmless.

rules.title: Site visit allowed
rules.text: Public Works must be allowed to observe at least one test session per permit term.

rules.title: Monthly test data
rules.text: Test data, including GPS and photos, goes to the City Administrator and Public Works every month.

rules.title: Monthly business list
rules.text: San Francisco businesses using the testing must be disclosed every month.

rules.title: Monthly incident report
rules.text: Violations, safety incidents, complaints, malfunctions, tampering and collisions must be reported every month.

penalties.text: Infraction against the permittee: up to $100, then $200, then $500 for repeat violations within a year. Staff cannot be criminally penalized.
Civil penalty of up to $500 per day, plus injunction and attorney's fees, through the City Attorney.
Administrative citation of up to $1,000 per day per violation, issued by Public Works.
Permit suspension or revocation. Revocation is mandatory for a significant safety risk and bars future permits.
